title: SimWorld: An Open-ended Realistic Simulator for Autonomous Agents in Physical and Social Worlds
abstract: SimWorld presents an open-ended realistic simulator for autonomous agents in physical and social worlds. Under the broadened boundary, it is worth screening as core because it combines explicit environments with cooperation and competition among agents.

title: A Context-Aware Onboarding Agent for Metaverse Powered by Large Language Models
abstract: This work studies a context-aware onboarding agent for the metaverse powered by large language models. It is a broadened-core candidate because the environment is explicit and the system centers on socially interactive situated assistance in immersive space.

title: An Open-Domain Avatar Chatbot by Exploiting a Large Language Model
abstract: This paper introduces an open-domain avatar chatbot built on a large language model. It should be screened as broadened-core because the interaction is avatar-based and socially situated rather than a purely disembodied text chat setting.

title: A Voice-Controlled Dialogue System for NPC Interaction using Large Language Models
abstract: This paper studies a voice-controlled dialogue system for NPC interaction using large language models. It is a broadened-core candidate because it places social interaction in an explicit game-world environment with identifiable NPCs.

title: Mixed-Initiative Dialogue Management for Human-Virtual Agents Interaction in Forum Theatre Inspired Training
abstract: This work focuses on mixed-initiative dialogue management for human-virtual-agent interaction in a forum-theatre-inspired training environment. It qualifies as a broadened-core candidate because the setting is socially interactive and spatially staged.

title: Large-language-model-driven agents for fire evacuation simulation in a cellular automata environment
abstract: This paper studies LLM-driven agents for fire evacuation simulation in a cellular automata environment. It is a broadened-core candidate because it combines explicit spatial constraints, situated multi-agent behavior, and socially relevant coordination under emergency conditions.

title: When agents learn to think: Large language model-enhanced agent-based modeling for crowd evacuation in disaster scenarios
abstract: This paper enhances agent-based modeling for crowd evacuation in disaster scenarios with large language models. It should be screened as broadened-core because the environment, movement, and collective behavior are all explicit.

title: CitySim: Modeling Urban Behaviors and City Dynamics with Large-Scale LLM-Driven Agent Simulation
abstract: CitySim models urban behaviors and city dynamics with large-scale LLM-driven agent simulation. It is a strong broadened-core candidate because it directly targets city-scale behavior in an explicit urban environment.

title: TongSIM: A General Platform for Simulating Intelligent Machines
abstract: TongSIM is a general platform for simulating intelligent machines in explicit virtual environments, including outdoor town scenarios. It is worth screening as broadened-core because the environment and social-interactive context are both explicit.

title: S^3: Social-network Simulation System with Large Language Model-Empowered Agents
abstract: S^3 is a social-network simulation system with large language model-empowered agents. It is a broadened-core candidate under the same digital-environment logic used for OASIS, since the structured social platform is the operative environment and collective behavior is central.

title: Unveiling the collective behaviors of large language model-based autonomous agents in an online community: A social network analysis perspective
abstract: This paper analyzes collective behaviors of LLM-based autonomous agents in an online community from a social network analysis perspective. It is a broadened-core candidate if structured digital communities remain admissible as environments in the core corpus.

title: Artificial intelligence chatbots mimic human collective behaviour
abstract: This paper shows that AI chatbots can mimic human collective behaviour in structured social settings. It should be screened as broadened-core if online social environments are retained as valid environments for the core corpus.

title: DeMAC: Enhancing Multi-Agent Coordination with Dynamic DAG and Manager-Player Feedback
abstract: DeMAC studies multi-agent coordination with dynamic manager-player structure and feedback in a shared interactive environment. It is a broadened-core candidate because coordination emerges in a common space rather than in isolated prompting.
